questiontext.text:
The figure below shows a trapezoidal prism. Calculate the volume of the prism.

[[jsxgraph]] var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard('jxgbox', { boundingbox: [-50, 350, 550, -50], keepAspectRatio: true, axis: false, showCopyright: false }); /* Front trapezium */ var A = board.create('point', [100,100], {visible:false}); var B = board.create('point', [300,100], {visible:false}); var C = board.create('point', [250,220], {visible:false}); var D = board.create('point', [150,220], {visible:false}); /* Back trapezium */ var E = board.create('point', [250,150], {visible:false}); var F = board.create('point', [450,150], {visible:false}); var G = board.create('point', [400,270], {visible:false}); var H = board.create('point', [300,270], {visible:false}); /* Front face */ board.create('polygon', [A,B,C,D], { borders:{strokeColor:'black'}, fillColor:'cyan', fillOpacity:0.4, vertices:{visible:false} }); /* Back face */ board.create('polygon', [E,F,G,H], { borders:{strokeColor:'black'}, fillColor:'cyan', fillOpacity:0.2, vertices:{visible:false} }); /* Prism edges */ board.create('segment',[A,E],{strokeColor:'black'}); board.create('segment',[B,F],{strokeColor:'black'}); board.create('segment',[C,G],{strokeColor:'black'}); board.create('segment',[D,H],{strokeColor:'black'}); /* Dimension labels */ /* Lower parallel side b */ board.create('text',[ 180, 80, '{#b#} cm' ],{ fontSize:14 }); /* Upper parallel side a */ board.create('text',[ 185, 235, '{#a#} cm' ],{ fontSize:14 }); /* Trapezium height h */ board.create('text',[ 85, 165, '{#h#} cm' ],{ fontSize:14 }); /* Prism length L */ board.create('text',[ 320, 120, '{#L#} cm' ],{ fontSize:14 }); [[/jsxgraph]]

Volume = [[input:ans1]] cm\(^3\) [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

To calculate the volume of a prism, first find the area of its cross-section and then multiply by the length of the prism.

For this question, the cross-section is a trapezium.

The area of a trapezium is:

Substituting the values from the diagram:

\(A=\frac{({@a@}+{@b@})\times {@h@}}{2}\) \(A={@cross_section_area@}\text{ cm}^2\)

The volume of the prism is:

Volume =\(\text{Area of cross-section}\times\text{Length}\) V=\({@cross_section_area@}\times{@L@}\) \(V={@ta@}\text{ cm}^3\)

Therefore, the volume of the trapezoidal prism is:

\({{@ta@}\text{ cm}^3}\)
